questions: explain how this bot works internally
answer: Embedding-based retrieval. Every question variant in my knowledge base gets encoded into a 384-dim vector once at load time. Your query is encoded the same way; cosine similarity picks the best match.

questions: what embedding model do you use
answer: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, quantized — about 23MB. Runs on CPU via Transformers.js with WASM.
No — every answer is hand-written by Pascal. I only pick which one matches your question best. No hallucinations possible.

questions: how many answers do you know
how big is your knowledge base
answer: Around 329 answer classes spread across faq.json (general chat), me.json (about Pascal), and website.json (the site itself), with ~1206 question paraphrases.
Each answer has several paraphrased questions. The closest paraphrase wins, which makes matching robust to how you actually phrase things.

questions: when do you say i don't know
how do you decide to answer
answer: If the top cosine-similarity score is below 0.45, I'll say I'm not sure rather than guess. You can see all top matches in the debug panel under the chat.

questions: why is the first load slow
why does it take time to load
answer: First visit downloads the ~23MB quantized model into your browser cache. After that it's instant — the model and the encoded knowledge base are cached.
Sub-100ms per query on a typical laptop CPU after the first load — most of the time is spent encoding your question into a single vector.

questions: how is inference done in browser
answer: I use Transformers.js (Xenova) running ONNX Runtime in WebAssembly. Pure CPU — no WebGPU, no server.
Yes — the project is called distilltiny (I'm Tini for short). Three small files (classifier.js, data.js, main.js) and three JSON files for knowledge.

questions: how do i add an answer

answer: Add an entry to one of the JSON files (id, category, questions[], answer) and reload. No retraining — embeddings are computed at page load.
Three files: faq.json (general chatbot questions), me.json (facts about Pascal), website.json (the site's easter eggs and design). All loaded together at startup.

questions: how do you find the best match
answer: Embeddings are L2-normalized, so cosine similarity is just a dot product. I score your query against every stored paraphrase and aggregate the best score per answer class.
No — each query is independent. There's no conversation state, and the model doesn't update from your inputs.

questions: what is the top matches panel

questions: why is the model so small
answer: Tiny means it ships and runs in a browser tab on a phone, with no server. Cosine similarity over good embeddings beats a big generative model for closed-domain FAQ.

questions: how big is the knowledge base
answer: About 76KB of JSON across the three files (faq.json ~51KB, me.json ~15KB, website.json ~10KB). Once embedded into 384-dim float32 vectors at load time, the index is ~1.8MB in RAM.
First load downloads ~23MB for the model + ~76KB of JSON knowledge. After caching, every subsequent visit is essentially free.

questions: does it work in other languages
answer: MiniLM is mostly English, but it has some cross-lingual ability — short questions in major European languages often still match.
